scope: Research reusing the actual Gemini in Google Chrome as a personal operator for the user's own website, not substituting a separate API chatbot.

conclusions.finding: Official Chrome auto browse documentation describes user-invoked, plan-reviewed multi-step website tasks, including on websites without a dedicated Gemini Connected App.
conclusions.qualification: Subject to real account/device/region/plan/rollout eligibility and confirmation. No test on the user's site occurred.

conclusions.finding: No public supported contract was found for an ordinary website to programmatically invoke the consumer Gemini in Chrome and receive arbitrary inference responses under its browser session entitlement.
conclusions.qualification: A documentation/source-research negative finding, not a mathematical impossibility proof or claim that every private interface was enumerated.

conclusions.finding: Gemini Apps Help documents connecting a personal/third-party app using its MCP server URL, then using it in the Gemini web and mobile apps.
conclusions.qualification: Help explicitly lists US, age 18+, personal account, English and Keep Activity. It does not establish India or Gemini-in-Chrome support. This is the agent invoking website tools, not the website invoking model inference.
conclusions.status: DOCUMENTED WITH SURFACE/REGION LIMITS; NOT RUN

conclusions.finding: WebMCP exposes page-side structured tools to WebMCP-aware agents; Chrome documentation describes origin-trial/local-development availability and testing clients.
conclusions.qualification: The primary I/O announcement says Gemini in Chrome will soon support it. Built-in consumer Gemini tool consumption was not live-verified, and inspector/API-key clients are not equivalent proof. Use optional progressive enhancement, not a guaranteed required dependency.
conclusions.status: EXPERIMENTAL; CONSUMER GEMINI CONSUMPTION NOT VERIFIED

conclusions.finding: The Prompt API uses a local Chrome model/Gemini Nano, distinct from the consumer Gemini in Chrome product.
conclusions.qualification: The fetched Prompt API page displays a future update label relative to the effective research date. Date-sensitive hardware/availability details require rechecking; earlier official I/O sources corroborate the product distinction.

conclusions.finding: Google documents Gemini Tasks/Spark and a Chrome integration, distinguishing local desktop Chrome from a separate remote browser and task/schedule surfaces.
conclusions.qualification: The July 30 announcement distinguishes international Spark access from the initially US Chrome integration. No 24/7 arbitrary website backend, unlimited quota or user-account availability is established.

documentation_conflicts.observed: Android availability and Android auto-browse Help list India and US. Desktop auto-browse eligibility still says US. Google One restrictions name India and US.
documentation_conflicts.resolution: Preserve all variants; do not infer availability for the user's particular account or device. Actual Ask Gemini / plan / Start Task / Let Gemini browse UI must be checked.

documentation_conflicts.observed: Android-specific auto-browse instructions exist, while shared desktop/tasks text says local Chrome auto browse is desktop-only and mobile uses a remote browser.
documentation_conflicts.resolution: Do not claim mobile local-session reuse. Record which browser instance is actually used in future acceptance.

documentation_conflicts.observed: Fetched auto-browse Help variants mention Plus/Pro/Ultra while some indexed variants mention Pro/Ultra only.
documentation_conflicts.resolution: No fixed plan/price/quota guarantee and no purchase recommended before account eligibility verification.

documentation_conflicts.observed: Browser API documentation and extension demos do not establish consumer Gemini-in-Chrome consumption; the official I/O wording is prospective.
documentation_conflicts.resolution: Treat WebMCP as experimental additive tooling and keep ordinary website UI functional.

documentation_conflicts.topic: Future labels relative to effective date
documentation_conflicts.observed: Fetched Prompt API page says updated 2026-10-21; Privacy Hub says 2026-10-26; Connected Apps Platform search result says 2026-11-03.
documentation_conflicts.resolution: Do not use those labels as evidence of already-shipped behavior/policy on 2026-10-19. The report records them explicitly and does not generalize future developer-platform pages to current Chrome/India eligibility.

proposed_security_acceptance: Use read-only then draft-only roles before public actions.
Authorize every backend operation and enforce tenant/resource ownership.
Keep model/tool inputs and external page content untrusted.
Do not treat tool hints, prompts, checkboxes or approved:true as independent human authorization.
Bind consequential approval to exact action/resource/diff and verified user interaction where necessary.
Require idempotency and durable receipts; a model completion statement is not proof of success.
Preserve TLS, sandbox, OAuth, Safe Browsing and origin/CSRF protections.
No Google session extraction, cookie replay, origin/brand spoofing or region/plan bypass.
Real user-account tests require user's own device/account with user present; no private-content captures.
